messages:
Anita: heads-up :rotating_light: after pushing runtime v3.2.1 to canary (10%) we're seeing p99 latency jump on gen endpoints for a handful of customers. p99 baseline ~220ms -> spikes to ~780-1.2s. p95 also up from 120ms -> ~340ms. Repro steps below, attaching logs. Can folks triage?

deploy-bot: rollout v3.2.1 -> canary (10%) initiated by Anita at 1865432098

Sasha: which model(s)/routes are hit? is this across all regions or single region? any correlation with sequence length?

Anita: mostly reported on `text-gen/redwood-base-30b` and `chat/redwood-instruct-7b` in us-west1. Not seeing region-wide — mostly us-west1 canary group traffic. Sequence len distribution similar to normal traffic (median ~64, 95th ~512).

Mike: saw similar spikes on our perf dashboards. quick snapshot:```
Time, p95(ms), p99(ms)
12:00, 115, 220
12:20, 130, 780
12:35, 142, 1020
12:50, 150, 1180
```

Tara: any config changes in this runtime? quantization kernel, scheduler, or batching defaults? I remember a batching scheduler refactor landed in this roll.

Anita: yes there was a change in the batcher heuristic (PR #4589) and a fallback kernel selector tweak that prefers mixed-fp paths for certain op shapes.

Sasha: can we bisect quickly? re: PRs in the release: batcher refactor, kernel selector, and a nvrtc change. If we can reproduce locally with canary image we can `git bisect` across the runtime commits.

Kevin: assigning myself. immediate mitigation options: 1) rollback canary to v3.2.0, 2) pin latency-sensitive customers to a stable instance pool, 3) temporary autoscale bump for canary to reduce queueing. Which do we want first?

Anita: CS already escalated — ticket from BigRetail reporting SLA breaches. We should rollback canary for safety and then bisect. Bump autoscale as mitigation while rollback goes.

CS-bot: ticket #CS-1124 created for BigRetail: "p99 regressions after canary rollout". Severity: P1. Customer experiencing request timeouts after 1s.

Mike: to help bisect, here's a small repro curl that hits the same code path (streaming enabled):```
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-base-30b","input":"<long prompt>...","max_tokens":256,"stream":false}' \
  -D - | grep -i x-request-id
```

Mike: also add `X-Trace-ID` header and capture runtimes from /metrics and request logs (we need `runtime.scheduler.latency` and `kernel.select.duration`).

Tara: for quick debugging, can we force the batcher into `static` mode using env override? I can push a canary env patch to turn off the heuristic so we can confirm if the batcher is culprit.

Anita: go for it. If that reduces p99 immediately, we have a smoking gun.

Kevin: doing rollback now for the canary group to v3.2.0. Rolling back 10% -> 0% over the next 2 minutes. Will monitor.

deploy-bot: rollback v3.2.1 -> v3.2.0 (canary) initiated by Kevin at 1865432180

Mike: post-rollback snapshot (10m after):```
Time, p95(ms), p99(ms)
12:55, 128, 360
13:05, 118, 240
```

Sasha: rollback helped, p99 trending back toward baseline but still slightly elevated vs pre-rollout. That suggests one of the canary changes caused the highest spikes. Queueing helped explain transient high tails.

Tara: Kevin, can you still enable the `static` batcher on a small canary replica (not traffic-facing) and run load to compare? I'll prepare a benchmark script to reproduce p99 diff.

Kevin: yes I'll spin a test harness. Also starting `git bisect` across the runtime commit range for the release. Using branch `release/v3.2.1`. Plan: bisect between tag `v3.2.0` and `v3.2.1` with our perf test.

Kevin: bisect commands:```
git checkout v3.2.0
git bisect start v3.2.1 v3.2.0
# at each step run: ./scripts/perf_smoketest.sh --model redwood-base-30b --qps 20 --duration 120
# mark bad/good with git bisect bad/good
```

Anita: while bisect runs, let's open a runbook entry for customers: temporary SLA exemption notice, and route BigRetail to a pinned pool. Tara, can you own that?

Tara: on it. Will pin their traffic to `pool-stable-02` and notify CS. Also adding a note to customers page about transient latency during canary rollouts.

Mike: FYI logs show `kernel.select.duration` spiking to 180ms on affected requests when p99 is hit. When we forced `static` batcher it dropped to ~20ms. That points to either a bad kernel selector path or interplay between batcher and kernel selection.

Sasha: good catch. Next step: reproduce the high `kernel.select.duration` locally with instrumentation enabled. If kernel selector is the culprit, we may revert that tweak instead of batcher.

Kevin: git bisect landed on PR #4612 (kernel selector fallback logic). Confirmed on local perf test: enabling old selector brings p99 down. I'll open revert PR and coordinate with release lead.

Anita: excellent. Plan: 1) revert kernel selector change (PR revert #4625), 2) re-deploy canary with reverted binary, 3) keep batcher heuristic toggled off until we validate. Kevin/Tara/Mike own deploy validation. Sasha will follow up with a postmortem root cause.

Kevin: created revert PR #4625 and started canary build. ETA 20m for canary rollout.

deploy-bot: PR #4625 merged by Kevin at 1865432289, new canary build pushed.

Mike: after merged revert and canary roll we're observing:```
Time, p95, p99
13:20, 118, 235
13:30, 115, 220
```

CS-bot: updated ticket #CS-1124: temporary mitigation applied, customer pinned to stable pool, ETA for full resolution 45m.

Anita: great work team. Follow-up actions: Sasha to write a short postmortem and attach perf graphs (due EOD). Kevin to run a full regression suite and validate no perf regressions for other models (due tomorrow). Tara to update runbook and customer comms (by EOD). Mike to add extra metrics around `kernel.select.duration` and `batcher.queue_depth` to the main latency dashboard.

Sasha: will draft postmortem. Initial hypothesis: kernel selector fallback introduced an O(n) scan for op shapes in some models causing occasional long selection times under certain batch shapes. Will include reproducer and recommended fix (optimize selector or use cache).

Anita: thumbs up :thumbsup: Please add links to PRs and dashboards in the thread when available. Closing the immediate escalation — reopening if we see more spikes.

Kevin: adding JIRA RT-2356 to track bisect/revert/validation and referencing CS-1124.

Mike: one last note — consider adding a pre-rollout perf smoke test for kernel selection on a small subset of models in CI to catch this earlier.

Tara: agreed, adding to backlog.

Anita: thanks all.
